questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to study in the States and also try a destination i knew had a great culture life, a professional faculty and an environment different from what we have in Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My experience was amazing! The only reason it is a 9 instead of 10 is the cost of living in the States. Even though New Orleans is more affordable than NYC, San Fransisco etc., it is incredibly expensive to live in the States.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The staff at Tulane University is extremely helpful and they provide a lot of helpful resources both before and after you arrive in New Orleans. Even though it is a good idea to  start researching housing on your own (for example on Facebook groups), they will give you plenty of information about your entire stay.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They offer an introduction to US law, where they provide a lot of information other than only law lectures. I would highly recommend attending this introduction as you both get practical information, free trips around New Orleans and get to know a lot of other international students from all over the world studying law.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through groups on Facebook. I would recommend finding housing on your own, off campus (as on campus is only provided for a limited time), but in the area called "uptown". That area is very close to campus and is very much a "campus" and "student" vibe.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would not recommend finding housing downtown. It is 45 min away from campus and you will most likely have lectures every or every other day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Pretty accessible registration with helpful link provided from the host university.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university reaches out to the students and therefor you automatically get a person to contact. They are extremely fast at replying (when you consider the 7 hour time difference).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register for courses as soon as possible, especially if you want to register yourself on some of their popular seminars. Choose whatever courses seem interesting to you and try some of the courses that arent provided in copenhagen! I can highly recommend legal research and writing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses I took were either the same level of what we have at Copenhagen University or easier. You have more courses, I had 5, but each course is only around 2.5, 5 or 7.5 ECTS.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The course depends on the professor. For example, even though several are three torts classes, every class can differ because of the professor. Even how the exam is (open book/closed book) can differ. In general 2L or 3L courses have a more "laid back" vibe, where the professors dont cold call the students as much.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Intro to Law of the US – 2 credits
International Human Rights Law – 3 credits
Constitutional Criminal Procedure: Investigation – 3 credits
Space Law: International Treaties and Jurisdiction – 1 credits
Legal Reasoning, Research and Writing for LLM Students – 3 credits

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Intro to Law of the US: Again, I HIGHLY recommend every exchange student to take this course. Time consuming for around 3-4 weeks, but you learn all the basics of the US system. 

Legal Reasoning, Research and Writing for LLM Students: a time consuming course at times, but a course that teach you how to research US Law. A very valuable course!

Space Law: International Treaties and Jurisdiction: Super interesting area of law! Tulane University wish to be a front runner in this area in the future.

questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fresh produce and food in super markets in general. The cost was around double of what i pay in copenhagen when i go to the supermarket.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Free access to their very big fitness center where they also have all kinds of classes (spinning, dancing etc.). Also a big variety of different clubs and events you can sign up for.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of cultural, athletic and social activities available. More than you would ever be able to attend to during your stay. There is always something to do, both on and off campus at Tulane University! You will get a Tulane mail, where  they will inform you about a lot of the events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can highly recommend attending to the sports events or any event involved with New Orleans culinary.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go downtown to explore the city during the weekend in the day time, and Bourbon street in the night time. Get food and go for shopping at Magazine St. Try the steam boat. See the cementaries. Go explore the city by the tram. Attend every carnival if possible! 

If you have the time, fly to areas in the States with their famous national parks. Zion national park and Grand Canyon are amazing!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: You will adjust in no time. I have never in my life met such sweet and loving people. Southern state sweetness is definitely a thing!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try find housing with American students if you wish to socialize with other than international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Americans are very sweet and outgoing. But talking about politics is not a go to if you do not know the person. In Denmark this is usually not too sensitive, but it can be in the States.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How sweet and caring people from New Orleans are. They truley care for you and they are so very proud people are visiting!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Plan out what you want from your stay. Do you really wanna put a lot oof effort into every class and experience how the library vibes are? Do you wanna deep dive into the New Orleans culture and visit all of the famous and hidden gems? Doo you want to network and attend every social event? It can be difficult to check off everything you want to do at your stay, so I would recommend future exchange students to be intentional about what they wish to get from their stay.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To get an insight into the American legal system and to experience how it is to study and have an everyday life in the States. Also, I have met incredible people along the way!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To relax and not stress about everything i wanted with my stay. You have either 4 or 5 months, you will have time to do what you want to do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
